01 Now — Vigía Nova

Where I’ve been focused full-time since leaving Evaluar.com.

Head of Technology · Founding engineer

Jun 2026 — Present · Vigía Nova Consultores, Bogotá

A multi-tenant SaaS that gives Colombian SMEs real control of their accounting, finances and tax deadlines — trial balances, financial statements, sector comparison and the tax calendar in one place.

My role

I joined as the first engineer and own the technology end to end: architecture, product engineering, infrastructure, security and releases — working directly with the founding partners on what gets built and why.

What I’ve built

  • Accounting core: Trial-balance ingestion, general ledger, balance sheet and income statement over the Colombian chart of accounts (PUC), isolated per company.
  • Alegra integration: Rebuilds a company's books from the Alegra API — journals, bills and payments — and keeps the account catalog in sync.
  • AI assistant on Claude: Tool-calling over the company's own figures, streamed over SSE, able to draw charts, with AI quotas per plan.
  • Sector benchmarking: ETL over Supersociedades open data to compare a company’s margins and ratios against its industry.
  • Taxes, roles and plans: Tax obligations and deadline calendar, per-company custom roles and permissions, plan ceilings and rate limits.
  • Platform and delivery: Docker, Nginx and PostgreSQL on a VPS; GitHub Actions to QA and production; backups, health checks, plus the marketing site and an internal sales CRM.

05 About

I like owning a problem from the data model to the screen a person actually uses — and then keeping it running.

My background is backend: Java and Spring Boot first, then Python, FastAPI and AI workflows with LangGraph and the Claude API. Today that means designing systems small teams can depend on — with tests, sensible infrastructure and releases nobody is afraid of.

Outside work I lead Universidad Distrital’s GNU/Linux group and volunteer with Colmena DAO. I care about pedagogy and digital sovereignty, and about leaving codebases easier to understand than I found them.
